thread:
Marco (runtime): quick sanity check — ran cross-region failover harness (us-west1 -> eu-west1) with replay + synthetic mix. dumping results and notes here.
Sophia (perf): please paste the exact harness command and config used. need seeds to reproduce.
Marco (runtime): command below, seed=2026, mix=70% replay/30% synthetic, kv_prefill=75% (so warm-ish).
```
./tools/run_harness.py --replay replays/2026-02-prod.json --synthetic-mix 0.3 --seed 2026 \
  --region-pairs us-west1,eu-west1 --failure-drain 30s --batch-distribution "p50:1,p75:2,p95:4" \
  --kernel-policy auto --kv-prefill 75
```
Devon (infra): thanks. what hardware across regions? identical instance types? network emulation?
Marco (runtime): both sides used n1-standard-32 + A100 equivalent. we enabled 20ms added latency on inter-region egress for eu-west to simulate load.
Rachel (sre): profiling snapshot attached in gist -> high tail in p99 when fallback model engaged. looks like kernel switch cost + KV miss storms.
Marco (runtime): short summary numbers: primary region p50=18ms p95=42ms p99=130ms; during drain when routed to fallback region p50=55ms p95=140ms p99=410ms. kv hit rate hovered 72% overall, dropped to 18% right after failover.
Sophia (perf): that's consistent w/ KV cache coldness. we should separate warm vs cold scenarios. apples-to-apples means: same model quantization, same kernel selection flags, identical batch distribution seeds, and identical request sequence.
Devon (infra): for network, use tc/netem on the local harness so both runs see same net conditions. also pin CPU governor and disable background cron jobs.
Rachel (sre): reproduced a perf regression: when kernel_policy=auto, runtime switched to fused-attn-v2 at seq_len 512 causing a short GC-like stall on first request (~200ms) while JIT/kernels warmed. toggling to kernel_policy=fallback-legacy removed the stall but increased steady p50 by ~6ms.
Marco (runtime): noted. we'll add an explicit kernel-warm step in harness: 100 short warmups to force kernel selection before measuring.
infra-bot: deploy: canary model-serving-1.14 with kernel-fix rolled to us-west1 at 2026-03-04T13:40Z :rocket:
Sophia (perf): on batching heuristics — current continuous-batching config uses 50ms aggregation cap. for low-latency routes that's too aggressive during drain (spikes). propose adaptive cap: decrease to 10ms when routing-latency>200ms.
Marco (runtime): good idea. add measuring metric: effective_batch_size distribution pre/post drain. we saw median batch size drop from 3 to 1.2 during failover which hurt throughput.
ops-oncall: next steps I suggest: (1) produce two reproducible harness configs: "warm-cache" and "cold-cache"; (2) add a deterministic replay-only run for apples-to-apples; (3) add kernel-warm step; (4) run a dedicated suite for model-fallback cost (track p50/p95/p99 + kv-hit-rate + kernel-switch-count).
Sophia (perf): +1. also track GPU utilization and per-kernel time via nvtx traces. attach a sample trace to the perf dashboard.
Marco (runtime): I'll open an RFC with configs and attach scripts + raw results. linking draft in a sec: https://go.redwood/rfc/serving-cross-region-harness-draft (internal).
Rachel (sre): small checklist: ensure same quantization (int8 vs fp16), disable dynamic quant fallback, record seed, and include both synthetic-only and replay-only runs.
Devon (infra): I'll script the tc/netem profile and share. will also create infra labels so we can filter by region pair in dashboards.
Marco (runtime): OK I'll run the two canonical runs tomorrow morning and post artifacts. thanks all :thumbsup:
